independent_review.text:
# Independent review: packed progress token fixture correction

The one-operator test-only patch is supported, subject to the integrating owner checking the current fixture source and re-running its intended current acceptance command. Patch SHA256 `f8c426d3c0dc14bc46813b17435885b96488388d2ce6d5644ff36b7ac18e6157`, qualification SHA256 `b81ae9387ba4ed3ec1d5090e17da73804706d69b5e5567a3be587e4734b50c31`, base `b6ef5d7d94a7a7a2b3d65beb8115ffd2e1223e5c`. The changed predicate asserts equality of legacy and current progress-bar default option token; it retains scoped location, consumer-provided color/mode, and escaped SVG location checks. The original Material 16.2.14 legacy progress-bar public API re-exports the current progress token, and the original legacy component injects that token. Equality therefore matches the historical identity restored by the already reviewed product change. The location check tests injection scope and is not a claim about location-token identity.

I verified every recorded qualification artifact hash and byte count, the actual shared tarball SHA256 `08dae37e775e2ab50457d820b3c7ae98114059012125781378cd36f05d8990e5`, and the retained three result bodies. All have the same 106 ordered case IDs and the same reported tar. Original inequality yields 104/106, corrected equality 106/106, and the distinct-token negative 104/106; both failures in each negative are the targeted progress case and its aggregate standalone-harness consequence, not two separate product defects. The corrected result has `progressLocationAndDefaults: true`.

The negative is an isolated consumer-source mutation, not a changed packed library: it substitutes a synthetic `InjectionToken` for the fixture's legacy token and consequently provides defaults under the wrong token. Its actual record reports unequal tokens, legacy fallback `primary`/`determinate`, and location-scope control true. I reconstructed the changed consumer source and matched its recorded hash `a74c67fb7eb46461703a2a176e2c6f1f2256f007fe5625b44834819c80932bca`. The negative therefore exercises both the equality and provider/behavior portions of the conjunction; it does not isolate either subcondition alone.

The retained runs used the same `--tarball`, have null coordinator run IDs and use the packed TestBed/JSDOM fixture, not a native browser or sealed `--run` acceptance. The earlier 31/31 Chrome progress family used a different artifact and remains historical supporting evidence. No independent expensive rerun, product edit, 21.x/x64, full matrix, security or release qualification is claimed.
